entries.name: Mission triggers
entries.summary: Character, time and phone calls can determine when the next story marker appears.
body: Switch among the three protagonists and check each map. Some missions need time to pass or an incoming call; moving to another area may help the call arrive.
Before troubleshooting, keep an older save. Rockstar suggests trying a new Quick Save slot and reloading it; this is a workaround, not a guaranteed repair.

entries.name: Mission Disrupted recovery
entries.summary: A missing marker after “Mission Disrupted” has a specific Rockstar workaround.
body: Leave the mission area until its marker returns. Call Downtown Cab Company, choose that mission as the destination and skip the ride.
Try the mission again after arrival. Keep your earlier save so repeated attempts do not replace your only known-good progress.

entries.name: Story property signs
entries.summary: Story properties are bought at their location, not through Dynasty 8.
body: Find a house icon with a dollar symbol on the pause-menu map. Visit it and approach the realty sign to read the purchase prompt.
Dynasty 8 being unavailable in Story Mode is intentional. Check the price and the current protagonist before committing to a purchase.

entries.name: Uncalculated Risk prerequisites
entries.summary: Dom’s final activity depends on completing the required parachute and base jumps.
body: Compare your completed jumps with the full checklist in Rockstar’s linked support article. The absence of a phone response alone does not identify the missing prerequisite.
Keep a named checklist rather than a total count: a repeated jump does not demonstrate that a different required jump is complete.

entries.name: Legacy → Enhanced Story save
entries.summary: PC Story migration transfers one selected save; it is not ongoing synchronization.
body: Upload the chosen save from Legacy, then download it in Enhanced using the intended linked Rockstar account. PC-to-console transfer is not supported by this process.
Check the selected progress carefully before downloading. Rockstar says a successful Enhanced download ends further Story migrations for that account; later Legacy progress stays separate.

entries.name: Three protagonists, three abilities
entries.summary: Michael, Franklin and Trevor have different situational abilities.
body: Michael slows gunfight time, Franklin slows time while driving road vehicles, and Trevor gains a combat damage advantage. The ability meter limits use.
Identify the active protagonist and available meter before planning around an ability. Check your own platform bindings rather than copying an Xbox button sequence to PC.

entries.name: Self Radio
entries.summary: The PC radio can play supported local music files.
body: Place supported non-DRM music in Rockstar Games → GTA V → User Music under Documents, then scan from Settings → Audio.
Sequential and Shuffle allow track skipping; Radio adds station-style segments and does not. Test a few files first before adding a large collection.

entries.name: Snapmatic upload status
entries.summary: Taking a photo and publishing it to Rockstar are separate actions.
body: On the documented PS4, Xbox One and PC versions, choose a photo in Pause → Gallery and use its upload control. A small R* mark indicates successful upload.
Review the selected image before publishing. Do not assume every photograph is automatically online, or that the same button applies to every platform.

entries.name: Blue Zone route planning
entries.summary: The white circle indicates the destination for the shrinking play area.
body: Check your position, the white circle and the phase timer together. Remaining in the damaging zone costs health; exact timing and damage depend on the current mode.
Choose a route with reachable cover before continuing to loot. Recheck the map after each circle change instead of following an old marker blindly.

entries.name: Attachment compatibility
entries.summary: An attachment only transfers when the replacement weapon supports it.
body: Gameplay settings control automatic attachment behavior for pickups and weapon replacement. Incompatible parts remain in the inventory rather than equipping to the new gun.
After changing weapons, inspect the actual slots and ammunition before leaving cover. A familiar sight in your bag is not proof that it is mounted.

entries.name: Emergency Pickup deployment
entries.summary: An aerial relocation item needs open space and a planned landing.
body: Deploy where the balloon has clear sky and no nearby obstacles, then attach before the aircraft arrives. During transport you can detach and parachute to a selected landing.
Passengers remain vulnerable. Check current mode availability and circle restrictions in-game; the linked introduction documents the mechanism, not today’s spawn pool.

entries.name: Aim/Sound Lab
entries.summary: Private training separates aiming practice from directional sound practice.
body: Use a Lab access point in Training Mode and select aiming or sound practice. Sound exercises ask you to identify where a played gunshot came from.
Keep volume and headphones consistent between attempts. Change one setting at a time and compare results so a better score has a useful explanation.

entries.name: Carry a knocked teammate
entries.summary: Carrying repositions a downed player; reviving is a separate action.
body: Approach without sprinting and use your Limited Interact binding to pick up or put down the teammate. Choose a clear landing space before carrying.
Check nearby threats and the zone first. After reaching cover, put the player down and perform the normal revive interaction if conditions allow.

entries.name: Reviving at the water surface
entries.summary: A knocked swimmer can be revived at the surface, not underwater.
body: Both players must remain above water during the revive. Submerging or moving too much cancels it; a downed player is still losing health.
Agree on a nearby surface position or shore before approaching. Water does not provide reliable protection from opponents, so reassess whether the rescue is possible.

entries.name: Deston fuel pumps
entries.summary: A usable pump refuels a stopped vehicle while the driver stays seated.
body: Stop near an undamaged pump and use the driver’s interaction prompt. Moving the vehicle or changing seats interrupts refueling.
Damaged pumps can explode and destroyed pumps cannot refuel. Choose the stopping position before approaching and leave once your fuel plan is satisfied.

entries.name: Screen and map pings
entries.summary: A visible marker helps a squad agree on one location.
body: Aim at the intended location and use your ping binding, or place a map marker. Verify the marker landed on the intended surface rather than something closer.
Update the marker when the situation changes. A location ping is a callout, not ongoing enemy tracking; pair it with a short description when useful.

entries.name: Rush: warning and shelter
entries.summary: Flickering lights and approaching sound warn of a dangerous passage through Hotel rooms.
body: Locate a usable hiding place when the warning appears, then enter before Rush reaches you. Listen for it to pass before leaving.
Do not rely on a fixed countdown or assume every flicker has the same cause. The dark Greenhouse and run modifiers change the available cues.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Seek: Hotel chase route
entries.summary: The Hotel chase rewards reading the route while continuing forward.
body: Follow Guiding Light at intersections and crouch through highlighted low openings. In the final hallway, avoid reaching hands and burning obstacles.
Stopping to loot or treating a wardrobe as the solution interrupts the escape plan. These notes cover the Hotel chase, not the Mines minecart sequence.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Screech: camera response
entries.summary: This threat calls for looking at the entity instead of looking away.
body: In dark Hotel rooms, react to the quiet audio and screen cues by looking around for Screech. Check above and below your normal eye line, then face it directly.
After it disappears, return attention to your route. Do not transfer this response to Eyes, which has a different viewing rule.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Hide: leaving shelter
entries.summary: A hiding place is temporary protection, not a permanent safe room.
body: Remaining hidden too long can trigger Hide and force you out. Watch the warning while also listening for the active threat outside.
Leave once the passage is clear, but remain ready for Ambush returning. Avoid memorizing one universal hiding duration because rooms and modifiers can change it.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Guiding Light
entries.summary: Blue guidance can point toward required objects and chase routes.
body: During Seek encounters, watch for the indicated door or low passage. When searching for an essential object, inspect highlighted locations rather than repeatedly opening the same containers.
Some modifiers reduce or remove hints. Check the run settings before expecting the same assistance shown in an ordinary Hotel walkthrough.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: The Library: symbol code
entries.summary: Books provide symbol–number pairs; the paper determines their order.
body: Collect the marked books while avoiding Figure, then inspect the desk’s Solution Paper. Use its five positions to arrange the corresponding numbers.
Record symbol pairs carefully rather than treating the collection order as the code. Enter the completed code at the exit and leave once it opens.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: The Electrical Room
entries.summary: The Hotel exit combines a search, a breaker puzzle and a final escape.
body: After the opening encounter, search for all ten breaker pieces while avoiding Figure. Unlock the breaker room and insert the collected pieces.
Solve the switch pattern shown by the panel, then head for the elevator when power returns. Treat collection, puzzle completion and reaching the exit as separate objectives.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Batteries and light charge
entries.summary: A battery replenishes compatible electronic lights, subject to available capacity.
body: Search containers and furniture surfaces while keeping your compatible light. After collecting a battery, check the charge indicator rather than assuming the light is now full.
A full light or missing compatible item can prevent pickup. This item is not the same as the Battery Pack found in other DOORS content.
facts: Roblox · DOORS · The Hotel · standard run

entries.name: Guide Depot
entries.summary: The in-game guide collects build recommendations for a selected Resonator.
body: Open Guide Depot from the Terminal and select a Resonator. Compare Echoes, weapons, upgrade priorities and teammates; some characters have multiple guides.
Choose recommendations that match your owned equipment and intended role. The official announcement warns that guide data may refresh late, so check the guide’s assumptions before spending materials.

entries.name: Echo presets and comparison
entries.summary: Save a named setup before experimenting with another Echo lineup.
body: In Echo Assembly, save the current setup as a preset. Select another preset and expand attribute comparison before applying it.
Name setups by their purpose, such as exploration or a particular team. Compare the complete setup rather than one attractive stat on a single Echo.

entries.name: Echo management rules
entries.summary: Automatic rules can protect matching drops or mark them for discard.
body: Open Data Bank → Data Merge → Echo Management. Rules can consider quality, COST, Sonata Effect and main stat; several plans may be active.
Test a narrow auto-lock rule on a new drop before adding discard rules. Review all active plans and their results before processing your collection.

entries.name: Terminal synthesis
entries.summary: Purification and Conversion solve different material shortages.
body: Terminal Synthesis offers Purification across material rarities and Conversion for supported materials within the same category and rarity.
Open the intended upgrade first, record the missing item and quantity, then inspect the recipe output before confirming. Do not convert ingredients needed for another planned upgrade.

entries.name: Region Guide
entries.summary: The map’s Region Guide helps find regional features and their unlock conditions.
body: Open the Region Guide from the map. Select an unlocked feature to navigate to it, or read the requirement shown for a locked feature.
Use this before searching random map icons for a missing activity. A visible region or feature does not mean its prerequisites have already been completed.

entries.name: Resonator Skill Training
entries.summary: A character tutorial helps connect inputs to the Resonator’s combat sequence.
body: Find Skill Training under Guidebook → Path of Growth and select the relevant Resonator. Follow the demonstrated sequence before testing it in a familiar encounter.
Practice one unclear transition at a time. Equipment recommendations alone do not teach when to switch characters or which input a skill requires.

entries.name: Ascension collection spots
entries.summary: Material tracking starts from the item you actually need.
body: Select an Ascension Material in Backpack or the Resonators page, then choose Collection Spots. After exhausting the tracked location, the next location becomes available for tracking.
Set a target quantity before leaving and check it after each stop. This is a gathering aid, not evidence that a resource has instantly respawned.

entries.name: Flight in Jinzhou and the Black Shores
entries.summary: Flight access in these regions depends on the Windrider Project tutorials.
body: Complete the required Flight tutorials before using the utility in Jinzhou or the Black Shores. Some areas near water or map boundaries switch Flight to Glide.
Test a short route after unlocking it and watch the current utility indicator. Do not plan a long crossing on the assumption that Flight works everywhere.

entries.name: Extraction conditions
entries.summary: An extraction marker may require payment, activation or specific equipment conditions.
body: Select the intended map and difficulty in the official map tool. Read the chosen exit’s condition before committing to a route.
Identify a second option and verify both against the current match map. A reference marker is not proof that an exit is available in your run.

entries.name: Supply-marker route planning
entries.summary: Filter the official map for the supplies your run needs.
body: The map tool separates supplies such as medical containers, safes and ammunition crates. Combine useful supply markers with extraction markers to plan a compact route.
A container marker describes a search location, not a guaranteed item. Stop adding detours when the remaining extraction time or carried loot makes the risk unattractive.

entries.name: Ammunition and armor interaction
entries.summary: Caliber compatibility and penetration are separate equipment checks.
body: Choose ammunition that fits the weapon, then inspect its penetration and damage descriptions. Armor changes how hits affect health and durability.
Budget ammunition together with the gun, rather than spending everything on attachments. Use current item values; this reference does not set a maximum tier or promise a fixed number of hits.

entries.name: Gear Ticket kits
entries.summary: A prepared kit reduces setup work but still needs a pre-deployment check.
body: Inspect the Gear Ticket’s weapons, armor, ammunition and medicine before using it. Read the restrictions shown by your client.
Pick one achievable objective that suits the supplied kit. Receiving a prepared loadout does not mean it matches every difficulty, mission or playstyle.

entries.name: HRTF directional audio
entries.summary: An audio setting can help distinguish directions and floors.
body: The official patch describes HRTF under Settings → Audio for directional, binaural sound. Compare it using the same headphones and volume.
Ask a teammate to move at known positions and floors, then compare on and off. Keep the setting that improves your own judgment; it is not automatic enemy tracking.

entries.name: Luna’s two arrow roles
entries.summary: Detection Arrow gathers information; Volt Arrow creates a damaging contact area.
body: Luna’s Detection Arrow emits pulses while flying to detect moving targets. Volt Arrow produces an electrical effect on contact with a surface.
Choose the arrow for the immediate question: checking movement or pressuring an area. A scan describes a moment; confirm the situation again before moving.

entries.name: Tactical Gear Supply
entries.summary: The consumable supports gadget recovery, with effects depending on the operator.
body: Read the item’s current description and your operator’s gadget status before using it. The official introduction distinguishes cooldown recovery from ammunition restoration for certain gadgets.
Use it when its listed effect will actually help, then confirm the indicator changed. Do not assume every operator receives the same recovery amount.

entries.name: Protect stored weapon builds
entries.summary: Loadout assembly can be prevented from dismantling weapons already in the stash.
body: Disable “Allow loadout to dismantle stash weapons” before assembling another loadout if you want to preserve stored builds.
Inspect the stored weapon before and after applying the new loadout. This setting protects against that assembly behavior; it does not replace checking purchases or your deployed gear.
